unit.why: A short anecdote: R. Yitzhak of Drohobych, lost on the road, performs a yihud that benefits the 'prince of the forest', who then carries him to his destination in an instant.

stories.start_quote: הה״ק החסיד ר׳ יצחק דראהביטשטר זצללה״ה
stories.summary_en: R. Yitzhak of Drohobych, lost on the way at night, performed a yihud that did a great favour for the prince of the forest, who in return brought him to his destination in the blink of an eye.

quotes: והי׳ מיחד יחוד א׳ וע״י היחוד

tags.why: He is carried to his destination in an instant.

quotes: פ״א הי׳ תועה בדרך ובא בלילה
tags.why: The tale turns on the tsaddik's journey and getting lost.

tags.why: He interacts with the 'prince of the forest', a spiritual being.
The forest prince may be a spirit or demon; this is ambiguous.
R. Yitzhak of Drohobych is a pre-Hasidic baal-shem-type figure.
The unification of names is used to bring about a concrete result.
